justification: S3 increment 1 — the contract drift check, the live tripwire on the S2 typed boundary. The S2 contracts tolerate a missing key (parses to None), so a service that RENAMES or DROPS a key silently nulls the brief card (the #589 class). check_drift(contract_cls, raw) compares a real service output's keys to the contract's expected fields: a MISSING contract field = a rename/drop (drift, dangerous), an EXTRA key = a new service field (informational). check_outputs runs it across flood/bushfire/shadow (shadow has no outputs wrapper). A CLI validates a captured-outputs JSON and exits non-zero on drift. Two modes: CI/regression against captured baselines (the tests), and live (a Railway cron captures each service's real output for a demo address, dumps JSON, runs this to fail on drift BEFORE a user hits a blank card). The pure functions are fully unit-tested; the live-capture step needs DB/network so it is documented for the cron, not shipped untested.

pre_impl.existing_data: The S2 contracts (FloodServiceOutput/BushfireServiceOutput/ShadowServiceOutput) expose their expected keys via model_fields; the brief parses tolerantly (missing key -> None).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A tolerant contract can't itself catch a rename at runtime (it just nulls); the drift check is the separate, scheduled tripwire that compares real keys to the contract.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New tool; complements the failsoft lint (commit-time) and the per-build contract tests (CI). Reuses the S2 contracts as the source of truth.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A drifted live output (rename/drop) is flagged with the exact missing key + a non-zero exit, so the cron surfaces it; an extra new key is reported but not failed.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Backend tooling only. 2295 tests pass incl 6 new drift tests.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a service rename silently nulled a card and was only found by a user noticing a blank. After: the scheduled drift check fails loudly the moment a service's keys diverge from the contract.

functions.name: check_drift
functions.input: a Pydantic contract class and one service output dict
functions.output: a finding dict with the missing contract keys (rename/drop = drift), the extra service keys (informational), and a drift boolean
functions.if_none: an empty or None output reports every contract field as missing (full drift)

functions.name: check_outputs
functions.input: a mapping of service name to its captured raw output
functions.output: per-service findings plus an overall has_drift flag, handling the shadow no-outputs-wrapper case
functions.if_none: an unknown service is reported with a note and no drift

values: N/A - contract key comparison, not regulatory values.
queries: N/A - no DB query in the pure checker; the live-capture step (documented) calls the services.

break_it.scenario: A service legitimately adds a new output key
break_it.what_happens: it must be reported as informational, not failed as drift
break_it.repro: an output with an unexpected extra key
break_it.how: extra keys go to `extra` and do not set `drift`. Guarded by test_no_drift_when_all_contract_keys_present

break_it.scenario: A service renames a key the brief reads (the #589 bug)
break_it.what_happens: it must be flagged as drift with the missing key named
break_it.how: the missing contract field is detected and the run exits non-zero. Guarded by test_drift_when_a_contract_key_is_renamed + test_check_outputs_flags_one_service_among_many

break_it.scenario: Shadow output is checked with the wrong wrapper assumption
break_it.what_happens: shadow could falsely show full drift
break_it.how: the registry marks shadow with subkey None so it is checked at the top level. Guarded by test_shadow_uses_no_outputs_wrapper

break_it.scenario: An all-None genuine-empty output is mistaken for drift
break_it.what_happens: a real 'nothing detected' run could fail the check
break_it.repro: outputs with every key present but None
break_it.how: drift is about key PRESENCE, not value; all-None with the right keys is no drift. Guarded by test_check_outputs_flags_one_service_among_many (bushfire/shadow all-None pass)

post_merge.other_repo: N/A - the live-capture cron (to be wired) would run in the Railway python service where the brief already runs.
post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/brief_contract_drift.py <captured.json> exits 0 on matching keys, 1 on a renamed/dropped key. Wire a Railway cron to capture each service's real output for a demo address and run it on a schedule.
